rows.question: Which valves must be closed to isolate T4750 for maintenance? List them in the order you would close them, explain the order, and say which connections this drawing does not let you isolate.

required.item: the line from SV 104.01 has no isolation valve

rows.answer:
Derived by graph analysis of the drawing
- GlobeValve 47123/C1 (GlobeValve-2) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47123, DN 80) [E1.2, isolation_boundary]
- GlobeValve 47127/C1 (GlobeValve-1) is the first valve on the upstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47127, DN 50) [E1.3, isolation_boundary]
- ButterflyValve 47124/C1 (ButterflyValve-1) is the first valve on the downstream side of T4750 (Tank-1) (line 47124, DN 80) [E1.4, isolation_boundary]
- Every connection of T4750 (Tank-1) ends at a shut-off valve, a relief device or a closed end (3 boundary valves: GlobeValve 47123/C1 (GlobeValve-2), GlobeValve 47127/C1 (GlobeValve-1), ButterflyValve 47124/C1 (ButterflyValve-1)) [E1.6, isolation_boundary]
- With the boundary valves treated as closed, T4750 (Tank-1) has no drawn path to a relief device [E1.7, isolation_boundary]

Summary (model wording; the lists above are what was checked)
The isolation boundary for T4750 lists three shut‑off valves: GlobeValve 47127/C1, GlobeValve 47123/C1 and ButterflyValve 47124/C1. Closing the upstream valves first stops flow into the tank, then closing the downstream valve isolates the tank from the rest of the system. The drawing shows no valve between T4750 and the relief device SV 104.01, so that connection cannot be isolated by valve closure.
